# Extension A — backup DNS failover
# machine: 10.7.13.238 (mac3-backend-a)   date: 2026-11-23 12:47:29 IST
# generated by: scripts/phase2/demo-dns-failover.sh


$ networksetup -getdnsservers 'Wi-Fi'
10.7.20.228
10.7.18.17

$ scutil --dns | awk '/^resolver #1/{f=1} f&&/nameserver\[/{print} /^resolver #2/{exit}'
  nameserver[0] : 10.7.20.228
  nameserver[1] : 10.7.18.17

$ dig app.paradise.test | grep -E 'ANSWER SECTION' -A1; dig app.paradise.test | grep SERVER
;; ANSWER SECTION:
app.paradise.test.	30	IN	A	10.7.3.123
;; SERVER: 10.7.20.228#53(10.7.20.228)
→ answered by the PRIMARY (10.7.20.228).

>>> ACTION: On Mac 1 (10.7.20.228) run:  make p2-dns-stop

$ dig +time=2 +tries=1 @10.7.20.228 app.paradise.test | grep -E 'connection refused|timed out|no servers|status' || true
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
→ the primary no longer answers.
(client DNS cache flushed, so the next lookup is a real one, not a cached hit)

$ dig app.paradise.test | grep -E 'communications error|ANSWER SECTION|SERVER' -A1
;; ANSWER SECTION:
app.paradise.test.	30	IN	A	10.7.3.123
--
;; SERVER: 10.7.18.17#53(10.7.18.17)
;; WHEN: Mon Nov 23 12:48:03 IST 2026
→ dig hit an error on 10.7.20.228 and fell through to the BACKUP (10.7.18.17).

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code} via %{remote_ip}  (name resolved by the backup)\n' https://app.paradise.test/api/status
HTTP 200 via 10.7.3.123  (name resolved by the backup)
DNS service failure  : name resolution stops ('Could not resolve host'), but
                       ping 10.7.3.123 still works — the IP layer is fine.
Application failure  : resolution WORKS (dig returns 10.7.3.123), TCP+TLS to the
                       edge WORK, but nginx returns 502 — the backend is down.
Different first-failing layer → different fix. That is the diagnosis skill.

$ ping -c2 -t3 10.7.3.123 | tail -2
2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0.0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max/stddev = 6.058/7.181/8.304/1.123 ms

>>> ACTION: On Mac 1 run:  make p2-dns-start     (restore the primary)

$ dig app.paradise.test | grep SERVER
;; SERVER: 10.7.20.228#53(10.7.20.228)
→ back on the primary (10.7.20.228).
